title: From First Mover to Blueprint: Lessons from Bhutan’s Decentralized ID
description:
As one of the first countries to implement self-sovereign identity at national scale – and the first to anchor its national digital identity system on Ethereum – Bhutan had few direct precedents to follow. Building on existing models and decentralized technologies, it had to rethink their application to national public infrastructure.

The discussion unpacks the technical, institutional and societal choices behind implementation – from Ethereum’s role and the transition from Polygon to the governance, legal and operational conditions required for success. It explores the challenges of building trust, driving adoption and ensuring inclusion, as well as the opportunities and tradeoffs for countries with different levels of digital infrastructure, institutional capacity and population scale.
abstract: What does it take to turn decentralized identity from technological innovation into national public infrastructure – and what can other countries learn from Bhutan’s pioneering experience? Bringing together the Geneva Research Lab for Digital Impact (GRL) at the University of Geneva and Bhutan’s National Digital Identity technical team, this fireside chat draws on independent research and first-hand implementation experience to explore the opportunities, challenges and tradeoffs of decentralized identity at national scale, offering practical lessons for governments and Ethereum builders.
